data_quality.crooked.title: Currency journals posted without the rate

reports.formula.md: CM = Revenue − Direct variable costs. What sales leave after costs that grow with revenue.
reports.formula.md_margin: CM margin = CM / Revenue × 100%. Not defined (n/a) when revenue is zero or negative.
reports.formula.gp1: GP1 = Revenue − Direct variable − Direct production. What directions earn before shared costs.
reports.formula.gp1_margin: GP1 margin = GP1 / Revenue × 100%. Not defined (n/a) when revenue is zero or negative.
reports.formula.gp2: GP2 = GP1 − Production overhead. Gross profit of the whole business after production costs.
reports.formula.gp2_margin: GP2 margin = GP2 / Revenue × 100%. Not defined (n/a) when revenue is zero or negative.
reports.formula.op: OP = GP2 − Administrative − Selling. Core business profit before taxes, interest and depreciation (EBITDA).
reports.formula.op_margin: Operating margin = OP / Revenue × 100%. Not defined (n/a) when revenue is zero or negative.
reports.formula.np: NP = OP + Income below EBITDA − Expenses below EBITDA. What the business keeps. Dividends do not reduce it.
reports.formula.np_margin: Net margin = NP / Revenue × 100%. Not defined (n/a) when revenue is zero or negative.
reports.formula.net: Net cash flow = Closing balance − Opening balance. How much cash was added in the period.
reports.formula.closing: Closing balance = Opening balance + Net cash flow. Reconciled with cash account balances.
reports.formula.unclassified: Unclassified = Net cash flow − (Inflows − Outflows by rows). Cash that bypassed articles: map the account to an article.

screen_help.accounts.title: Chart of accounts
screen_help.accounts.body:
The chart of accounts is the list of shelves every rouble and every debt is placed on. Each operation lands on one of them, and the reports are built from there.
The product set this list up for you, and day-to-day work does not touch it: it is a bookkeeper's tool, not an owner's. Come here when you need a new account, or to understand why an amount landed somewhere unexpected.
If you only want your bank accounts and cash, that is the neighbouring screen, not this one.
screen_help.acquiring.title: Card payments
screen_help.acquiring.body:
Taking money by card: the customer pays, and the bank transfers the money to you less its fee, usually the next day.
This screen reconciles two figures that almost never match: what the customers paid and what the bank sent. The difference is the fee, and that is what most often gets lost.
Once this is set up, you stop unpicking bank transfers by hand.
screen_help.ai_chat.title: Ask about your money
screen_help.ai_chat.body:
Ask about your money in ordinary words: how much did I earn in July, what took the most money, will I make it to the end of the month.
The answer is worked out from your data, not invented. If there is not enough data, the product says so instead of producing a pretty number.
This does not replace the reports — it is a shortcut to them: the answer almost always links to the screen where the same thing is laid out line by line.
screen_help.all_transactions.title: Operations
screen_help.all_transactions.body:
Every movement on your accounts is here. The labels next to the amount describe the state: «owed to us» means you delivered but were not paid; «we owe» means you received the document but have not paid; «overdue» means the due date has passed.
The totals row is pinned at the bottom: how many operations made it into the selection and for how much. It follows any filter.
Transfers between your own accounts are not in the total: the money did not arrive or leave, it just moved.
screen_help.bank_api_sync.title: Bank connection
screen_help.bank_api_sync.body:
A direct link to the bank: statements arrive on their own, with no file uploads.
Once connected, operations show up within the day and wait for you to say what the money was for. You still categorise, but you no longer hunt for files.
The connection is made once per bank account and can be switched off here at any time.
screen_help.bank_rules.title: Statement rules
screen_help.bank_rules.body:
A rule is a pre-recorded answer to «what was this money for». For example: if the payment description contains «rent», use the «Rent» article.
Rules sort the statement for you. The more of them there are, the fewer lines are left to sort by hand, and the sooner the reports add up.
A rule can be created straight from the statement: sort a similar operation once, then ask the product to always do it that way.
screen_help.bills.title: Supplier bills
screen_help.bills.body:
Bills that were issued to you. Until a bill is paid it is your debt, and it shows in the reports and in the payment calendar.
Overdue items are visible here too: the due date has passed and the money has not left. Deal with those first — your supplier relationship depends on it.
A payment is attached to a bill rather than entered separately, so the debt closes itself instead of hanging twice.
screen_help.budgets.title: Budgets
screen_help.budgets.body:
A budget is a plan by article for a period, with the actuals shown next to it.
Look at «completed» together with «time elapsed», not on its own. Spending nine tenths of the budget in two thirds of the year is an overrun, even if the figure is not red yet.
If there is no plan for an article, the ratio is not calculated: there is nothing to divide by, and the product writes «n/a» instead of inventing a number.
screen_help.capitalization.title: What the business is worth
screen_help.capitalization.body:
A rough estimate of what the whole business is worth: how much profit it makes and what that turns into at the multiples used in the trade.
It is a starting point for a conversation with an investor or a partner, not a sale price. The real price is always negotiated and depends on who is buying.
The figure follows the profit: if profit jumps around, so does the estimate, and that is not an error.
screen_help.cash_flow_articles.title: Cash flow by articles
screen_help.cash_flow_articles.body:
This report answers «where the money came from and where it went». It counts actual movement, not accruals: what really passed through the accounts.
The three sections are about the nature of the movement. Operating is the ordinary work, investing is what you buy for the long run, financing is loans and the owner's money.
The «not assigned to any article» line shows money that went past the articles: if it is not zero, link accounts to articles.
screen_help.cashflow_accounts.title: Cash and bank accounts
screen_help.cashflow_accounts.body:
Every place your money sits: bank accounts, the cash box, the owner's card.
The total of the balances here is the answer to «how much money do I have right now». The same figure sits in the product header on every screen.
An account can be closed to new operations without being deleted: its past operations stay in the reports, and it stops appearing in pick lists.
screen_help.cost_allocation.title: Shared cost allocation
screen_help.cost_allocation.body:
Some costs cannot be pinned to one deal: rent, bookkeeping, advertising. These are shared costs, and without them deal profit looks better than it is.
Here you set the rule for splitting such costs between deals or directions: equally, by revenue, or by a share you choose.
After allocation the deal card shows a second profit figure, one that includes shared costs. It is the honest one.
screen_help.credit_notes.title: Customer credit notes
screen_help.credit_notes.body:
A credit note records that you owe a customer money back, or that it will be set against future purchases. In plain words, a return from the customer's side.
A return reduces the revenue of the period it happened in. Without the document, revenue stays overstated and the report shows an unexplained cash minus.
A credit note can be set against a new order, in which case no money leaves the account at all.
screen_help.credits.title: Loans and borrowings
screen_help.credits.body:
All money taken on loan: bank credit, borrowings from partners, instalments.
The main thing this screen gives you is the schedule ahead. It feeds the payment calendar, so a future instalment stops being a surprise.
A loan received is not revenue, and a repayment is not a cost. Profit does not change: cash and debt do.
screen_help.crm_integration.title: Sales system link
screen_help.crm_integration.body:
Pulls deals and contacts from your sales system so you do not enter them twice.
Once linked, a deal created by a salesperson appears here on its own, ready to show money and profit.
The link is one way: the product reads your deals and changes nothing on your side.
screen_help.customers.title: Customers
screen_help.customers.body:
The people who pay you. The list shows each one's debt: how much is owed in money and how much will be settled by delivery against an advance already received.
These two cannot be added together. Money arrives in the account; an advance has to be worked off. Added together they promise more cash than will actually come.
The customer card gathers the whole history: invoices, payments, deals and document correspondence.
screen_help.data_quality.title: Data quality
screen_help.data_quality.body:
A list of the places where the books leak: operations with no article, unlinked accounts, duplicate contacts, negative stock.
Every line is an amount that did not reach a report, or reached the wrong one. While the list is not empty, it is too early to trust the reports.
Lines can be cleared one at a time from here: each one leads to where it can be fixed.
screen_help.deals.title: Deals
screen_help.deals.body:
A deal is a single job or order with its own profit: a site refurbishment, a batch delivery, a client project.
The two ratios next to the amount answer different questions: «paid» is how much money has arrived, «delivered» is how much work has been handed over. The gap between them is the risk.
For deal profit to be true, a share of shared costs has to reach it too — that is done on the allocation screen.
screen_help.debts.title: Debts
screen_help.debts.body:
Every debt in one place: who owes you and whom you owe.
Debt in money and debt in work are kept apart. «The customer has to pay» and «we took an advance and owe the work» are different obligations, and adding them together misleads.
The age of the debt sits next to the amount: overdue items are worth clearing first, they cost the most.
screen_help.directions.title: Directions
screen_help.directions.body:
A direction is a simple label you sort money by: «retail», «wholesale», «the Lenin street site».
The label goes on an operation, and after that the reports can be read for each direction separately. That shows which one feeds the business and which lives off it.
A direction is not a deal. A deal ends; a direction runs for years.
screen_help.dividends.title: Owner's draws
screen_help.dividends.body:
Money the owner takes out of the business.
This is not a cost: profit does not go down. Cash and retained profit do. Recording a draw as a cost understates profit and gets the tax wrong.
The screen also shows how much has been taken over the year — a figure nobody usually remembers.
screen_help.estimates.title: Quotes
screen_help.estimates.body:
An offer to a client before they agree: what you will do, for how much and on what terms.
Until a quote is accepted it affects neither cash nor profit. An accepted quote becomes an invoice with one click, without retyping the lines.
Mark the refusals: they show at which stage and why clients walk away.
screen_help.expenses.title: Expenses
screen_help.expenses.body:
Spending with no supplier document behind it: cash purchases, small items, payments from the owner's card.
Every expense needs an article — the answer to «what for». Without it the money leaves the account but appears nowhere in the profit report.
Do not record a machine or a long-lasting refurbishment here: that is an investment, not a cost, and it belongs under fixed assets.
screen_help.expenses_analysis.title: Expense analysis
screen_help.expenses_analysis.body:
Where the money goes: costs by article, largest first, with each article's share.
The «not assigned» line shows spending with no article. While it is not zero the picture is incomplete, and the biggest costs may be hiding exactly there.
Any amount can be opened down to the operations it is made of.
screen_help.financial_model.title: Financial model
screen_help.financial_model.body:
A look ahead: what happens to cash and profit if sales grow or fall, if you raise the price or hire someone.
The model does not predict — it works out the consequences of your assumptions. Change an assumption and you see what it costs.
The most useful figure here is the point where the business turns positive: how much you have to sell to cover every fixed cost.
screen_help.financial_ratios.title: Key figures
screen_help.financial_ratios.body:
A handful of numbers used to judge the health of a business: return on what is invested, the share of your own money, how fast debts come back.
A figure on its own says little — what matters is how it moves. That is why the previous period always sits next to it.
When a figure cannot be worked out the product writes «n/a», not zero: zero would read as «bad» when there is simply nothing to divide.
screen_help.financial_reports.title: All reports
screen_help.financial_reports.body:
Every report in the product, each with a line on the question it answers.
Three matter most: profit and loss says whether you earned; cash flow says where money came from and went; the balance sheet says what you own and what you owe.
Profit and cash almost never match, and that is normal: delivered in May, paid in July.
screen_help.fixed_assets.title: Fixed assets
screen_help.fixed_assets.body:
Expensive things that last: a machine, a vehicle, a refurbishment.
Buying them is not a cost but an investment: the money left, and a thing arrived in its place. It turns into cost gradually, a little each month, for as long as it serves.
Recording a machine as an ordinary cost makes the month of purchase show a loss that never happened.
screen_help.inventory_adjustments.title: Stock adjustments
screen_help.inventory_adjustments.body:
Bringing stock figures in line with what is actually there: after a count, damage, a shortfall or a find.
An adjustment moves both stock and profit: a shortfall is a cost, a surplus is income. So it is not something to do casually.
Write the reason on every adjustment: in six months nobody will remember where the difference came from.
screen_help.invoices.title: Customer invoices
screen_help.invoices.body:
Invoices you issued. An issued invoice is already revenue on the accrual basis, even before the money arrives.
Unpaid invoices add up to what customers owe you and feed the payment calendar as expected inflows.
Overdue ones are shown apart: that is money you have already earned but not yet received.
screen_help.items.title: Items
screen_help.items.body:
The goods and services you sell and buy.
An item remembers its price and its article, so invoicing does not mean retyping them — and the amounts always reach the same report line.
Goods have stock, services do not: a service cannot be counted and put on a shelf.
screen_help.legal_entities.title: Legal entities
screen_help.legal_entities.body:
If the business runs through more than one company, they are listed here.
Reports can be read one entity at a time or all together. In the second case the product removes transfers between your own entities — otherwise the same money would be counted twice.
The entity is set on the account and fills itself into operations.
screen_help.make_journal_entry.title: New journal entry
screen_help.make_journal_entry.body:
A manual record for cases with no ordinary document: fixing a mistake, moving an amount, an accrual.
An entry always has two sides for equal amounts: from where and to where. If the sides do not meet, the product will not save it.
Use this rarely. If the same thing has to be typed in by hand every month, there is probably an ordinary document for it.
screen_help.management_articles.title: Accounting articles
screen_help.management_articles.body:
An article answers the question «what was this money for». You pick it when you categorise an operation, and the product uses it to decide which report line the amount lands in.
There are five kinds. Income and expenses take part in profit. Assets, liabilities and equity do not: buying a machine is an investment, not a cost, and a loan is not revenue.
If you are unsure, open the «Where it lands» tab: it shows where the amounts of the selected article will end up.
screen_help.manual_journals.title: Journal entries
screen_help.manual_journals.body:
Every record made by hand rather than by a document.
Look here when reports disagree: more often than not the cause is a manual record with no article or with the sides swapped.
An entry can be reversed but not rewritten after the fact: a reversal leaves a trace, a quiet edit does not.
screen_help.marketplaces.title: Marketplaces
screen_help.marketplaces.body:
Loading the reports of the platforms you sell through.
A platform sends one figure for the week, and inside it are sales, returns, commission, delivery and penalties. Until that is unpicked, revenue looks understated and the commission is invisible.
After loading, each part lands on its own article and the profit per platform becomes real.
screen_help.moysklad.title: Stock system link
screen_help.moysklad.body:
A link to your stock system: items, balances and shipments are brought across.
It saves double entry and keeps stock and money from drifting apart.
The transfer runs one way: the product reads the stock system and changes nothing in it.
screen_help.onec_export.title: Export for the bookkeeper
screen_help.onec_export.body:
A file for your bookkeeper: the period's operations in the shape their accounting program expects.
The export does not change your data, it only copies it. Run it as often as you like.
Check data quality first: operations with no article will still export, but your bookkeeper will have to sort them out.
screen_help.onec_import.title: Import from accounting software
screen_help.onec_import.body:
Loading a statement or operations from an accounting program, if the books are also kept there.
The product checks what is loaded for duplicates: the same operation will not land twice, even if the file is loaded again.
Lines that could not be read are listed with the reason, so they can be fixed and loaded again.
screen_help.payment_calendar.title: Payment calendar
screen_help.payment_calendar.body:
The calendar shows what happens to the money next: planned inflows are added to the account balance and outflows are subtracted.
If the balance goes negative somewhere, that is a cash gap. The product names the day, the depth and the day it ends, so you have time to borrow or move a payment.
At a scale coarser than a day, fact and plan sit in one column: the past part of the period has already happened, the rest is a forecast.
screen_help.payment_requests.title: Payment requests
screen_help.payment_requests.body:
A colleague asks for a bill to be paid, and you agree or refuse. Spending stops being a surprise.
An approved request enters the payment calendar as a future outflow before any money moves.
Who approved it and when stays in the request's history.
screen_help.payments_made.title: Payments to suppliers
screen_help.payments_made.body:
Money that went to suppliers. A payment is attached to a supplier bill and closes the debt behind it.
One payment can close several bills, and one bill can be paid in parts. The product keeps the remaining debt itself.
A payment with nothing attached leaves the debt hanging although the money has gone.
screen_help.payments_received.title: Payments received
screen_help.payments_received.body:
Money that arrived from customers. A payment is attached to an invoice and closes the customer's debt.
If more arrives than was invoiced, the excess becomes an advance: the customer has paid ahead and you now owe them work.
Unattached payments are shown apart — they are the commonest reason a customer's debt does not add up.
screen_help.payroll.title: Payroll
screen_help.payroll.body:
What is owed to staff and what has been paid to them.
Accrual and payment are separate events. Accrued at the end of the month, paid at the start of the next: profit falls in the first month, cash leaves in the second.
Payroll taxes and contributions are separate lines: they are not the same thing as the wage itself.
screen_help.receipts.title: Till receipts
screen_help.receipts.body:
Sales for cash or card without an invoice: retail, a café, services on the spot.
A receipt is both revenue and cash at once: no invoice is needed behind it.
If you take cards, the money arrives later from the bank and less the fee — that is unpicked on the card payments screen.
screen_help.tax_rates.title: Tax rates
screen_help.tax_rates.body:
The rates that fill themselves into documents: VAT and the rest.
A rate is set once and then picked from a list, so no stray numbers appear in invoices.
If you work without VAT, keep the «No VAT» rate: it has to be chosen explicitly too, otherwise the printed form comes out blank.
screen_help.transactions_locking.title: Period locking
screen_help.transactions_locking.body:
Closing a past period: once closed, its operations can no longer be changed.
This guards against the most galling error — a filed report that stops matching the product because someone edited last month.
The lock date can be moved back, but that shows in the history: the past cannot be changed quietly.
screen_help.vat_analysis.title: VAT overview
screen_help.vat_analysis.body:
How much VAT you charged on sales and how much you can reclaim on purchases. The difference is what you will have to pay.
Lines with no rate are shown apart: while they exist, the amount payable is not exact.
This is a prompt for the conversation with your bookkeeper, not a finished return.
screen_help.vendor_credits.title: Supplier credits
screen_help.vendor_credits.body:
A document recording that a supplier owes you money back, or that it will count against a future delivery.
The credit reduces the costs of the period it happened in. Without the document costs stay overstated and money from the supplier looks like revenue.
A credit can be set against a new delivery, in which case no money moves at all.
screen_help.vendors.title: Suppliers
screen_help.vendors.body:
The people you pay. The list shows the debt to each one: how much is owed in money and how much the supplier owes you in delivery against an advance already paid.
These two cannot be added together. The first will take money out of the account; the second will not.
The supplier card gathers the whole history: bills, payments and credits.
screen_help.warehouses_transfers.title: Stock transfers
screen_help.warehouses_transfers.body:
Moving goods from one warehouse to another.
A transfer changes neither profit nor cash: the goods are the same, they just sit elsewhere. Only warehouse balances move.
Goods in transit count as sent but not yet received, so they never show in both places at once.
screen_help.zenmoney.title: Personal spending link
screen_help.zenmoney.body:
A link to a personal finance app that brings across spending made on a personal card.
In a small business part of the costs never pass through the bank account. Until they are counted, profit looks bigger than it is.
Personal spending unrelated to the business should not be brought across — leave it in the app.

data_quality.drifted_balances.title: Account balance drifted from its ledger entries
data_quality.drifted_balances.descriptio: The product keeps each cash account's balance in two places: on the account itself — shown in the header and on the home screen — and in the ledger entries the reports are built from. While they agree, nobody notices. When they drift apart, one screen contradicts another and there is nothing left to tell you which is right.

data_quality.drifted_balances.total: Total drift: {amount}. That is exactly how far the header's total balance is from the ledger.
data_quality.drifted_balances.hint: The product does not fix this on its own: which figure is right is your call. The stored balance may have fallen behind the ledger, or it may correctly hold opening money the ledger never received. Open the account and check it against the bank statement.
